name: Sharky's Woodfired Mexican Grill
tagline: Track calories and macros for Sharky's organic burritos, power plates, and tacos.
description: Track calories and macros for Sharky's organic burritos, power plates, and tacos.
articleHtml:
Sharky’s nutrition depends on more than choosing a burrito, taco, or bowl.

The menu combines different proteins, rice and bean choices, tortillas, grilled vegetables, guacamole, sour cream, cheese, sauces, and sides. Power Plates work differently from burritos, tacos can use different proteins and preparations, and current menu items include everything from wild-caught seafood to Wagyu beef.

Use the Sharky’s Woodfired Mexican Grill Nutrition Calculator above to match the meal you actually order and track its available calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, fiber, sugar, and sodium.

Start With the Type of Meal

Sharky’s current restaurant menu spans several distinct ordering formats, including:

Burritos

Tacos

Power Plates & Bowls

Classics

Salads & Soup

Plant-Based Meals

Kids Meals

Sides & Extras

Family Meals

and current featured items.

Those formats should not all use the same calculation logic.

A Fiesta Burrito is a finished tortilla-based meal. A Power Plate is built around a protein plus selected sides. A taco can use a different tortilla and protein preparation. A family meal contains group-sized portions.

Choose the format first.

Sharky’s Is More Than a Burrito Chain

Sharky’s describes its food around organic, natural, and locally sourced ingredients where available. Current brand information highlights:

natural chicken breast

grass-fed steak

wild-caught fish

organic tofu

organic black and pinto beans

non-GMO rice

organic corn tortillas and chips

and organic salad greens.

These ingredients are used across several menu formats, so the calculator should connect the same protein or side component to each compatible meal rather than maintain unrelated duplicate values.

Burritos Need the Exact Recipe and Protein

The current ordering menu still includes core burritos such as:

Fiesta Burrito

Sharky’s Burrito

Santa Fe Burrito

Fajita Burrito

Wild Caught Salmon Burrito

Wild Caught Fish or Shrimp Burrito

Organic Bean & Cheese Burrito

AJ Burrito

and current featured burritos.

Each recipe uses a different combination of rice, beans, cheese, guacamole, sour cream, vegetables, seafood, and sauces.

Do not reduce the entire burrito menu to:

tortilla + protein .

The complete recipe matters.

Fiesta Burrito Includes Several Calorie-Dense Ingredients

The current Fiesta Burrito includes:

protein

non-GMO rice

organic beans

Jack and cheddar cheese

guacamole

sour cream

and salsa.

Changing only the protein does not remove the calories from rice, cheese, guacamole, or sour cream.

NutritionSolver should therefore let the user choose the Fiesta Burrito first, then select the actual protein and supported customizations.

Sharky’s Burrito Is a Simpler Recipe

The current Sharky’s Burrito uses:

protein

non-GMO rice

organic black beans

and salsa.

It does not contain the same standard combination as the Fiesta Burrito.

That difference should remain visible instead of treating both as one generic burrito with different names.

Santa Fe Burrito Has a Different Base Again

The current Santa Fe Burrito centers on:

protein

cheese

guacamole

and:

pico de gallo .

Its recipe structure is clearly different from both Fiesta and Sharky’s burritos.

Use the published complete recipe as the starting point and then adjust for customer modifications.

Fajita Burrito Makes Vegetables Part of the Core Recipe

The current Fajita Burrito includes:

grilled vegetables and onions

non-GMO rice

organic beans

guacamole

and:

pico de gallo .

That means the grilled vegetables are not merely an optional topping.

If a user removes or substitutes them, the calculator should treat that as a modification to the standard recipe.

Wild Caught Salmon Has Its Own Finished Burrito Recipe

Current ordering menus describe the Wild Caught Salmon Burrito with:

grilled wild Alaska salmon

furikake seasoning

teriyaki nori brown rice

avocado

cucumber

shredded cabbage

sesame chili aioli

and a whole-wheat tortilla.

This is not simply:

salmon + tortilla .

The rice preparation, avocado, aioli, and other ingredients all contribute to the finished nutrition.

It deserves a separate recipe record.

Fish and Shrimp Need Preparation Choice

Sharky’s currently offers grilled and battered seafood options across burritos and tacos.

Current taco options include:

Grilled Wild Caught Fish

Grilled Shrimp

Baja Wild Caught Fish

and:

Baja Shrimp .

Grilling and battering do not produce identical nutrition.

The calculator should ask:

Fish or Shrimp → Grilled or Baja/Tempura

before applying the rest of the taco or burrito recipe.

Tacos Need More Coverage Than Traditional Chicken and Steak

Sharky’s current taco menu now includes newer recipes such as:

Wagyu Smashburger Taco

Fire Hot Wagyu Smash Burger Taco

Chicken Tinga

Achiote Chicken

Crispy Cheese Fiesta Taco

alongside fish, shrimp, Original, California, and other established taco styles.

These should be searchable by their actual names.

A customer searching for a Wagyu Smashburger Taco should not be forced to approximate it using an old steak taco record.

Current Wagyu Items Need Immediate Coverage

Sharky’s official homepage is currently promoting two new products:

Wagyu Philly Burrito

and:

Fire Hot Wagyu Smash Burger Taco .

The Wagyu Philly Burrito combines Wagyu beef, Cooper Sharp white American cheese, crispy potatoes, poblano queso, sweet and poblano peppers, caramelized onions, a toasted tortilla, Cholula, and sesame.

That recipe is too different from an ordinary steak burrito to reuse old steak nutrition.

If Sharky’s interactive calculator does not yet publish a verified nutrition result for the new item, use:

Nutrition not yet available

rather than estimating it from another burrito.

Fire Hot Wagyu Is a Separate Current Taco

The Fire Hot Wagyu Smash Burger Taco adds jalapeño and Cholula to the Wagyu taco concept and is currently featured by Sharky’s.

Treat:

Wagyu Smashburger Taco

and:

Fire Hot Wagyu Smash Burger Taco

as two separate recipes.

Do not assume the spicy version has identical sodium or carbohydrate values.

Power Plates Need Their Own Builder

Power Plates are one of Sharky’s most distinctive menu formats.

Historically and in current menu listings, customers choose a protein and then choose sides rather than receiving one fixed complete plate. Current menu listings continue to show chicken, steak, salmon, shrimp, tofu, and other Power Plate or Power Bowl options.

The correct calculator model is:

Protein → Portion → Side 1 → Side 2 → additional side where applicable

rather than one fixed “Power Plate calories” record.

Half and Full Power Plates Must Remain Different

Sharky’s historical official menu clearly distinguished:

Half Power Plate

and:

Full Power Plate ,

with different protein amounts and a different number of included sides.

If the current ordering system still supports those serving formats at a selected restaurant, keep them separate.

Do not calculate a Full plate by blindly doubling a Half plate because side count and portions may not scale uniformly.

Power Bowl and Power Plate Should Not Be Confused

Current restaurant listings also show Power Bowls built with ingredients such as:

brown rice

beans

spinach

steamed vegetables

avocado

and the selected protein.

That is a specific bowl recipe.

A Power Bowl should not automatically inherit the same nutrition as a Power Plate with user-selected sides.

Use distinct menu formats.

Salmon Power Bowl Needs Recipe Context

NutritionSolver currently lists a Power Bowl Salmon at 430 calories.

But a current Salmon Power Bowl listing describes salmon together with brown rice, beans, spinach, steamed vegetables, and sliced avocado.

That means any nutrition record should clearly state whether the 430 calories represent:

the complete current bowl

or:

a protein-only / previous recipe configuration .

Do not publish the value without validating the current recipe against Sharky’s own interactive nutrition calculator.

Side Choice Deserves First-Class Treatment

Sharky’s current side offerings include choices such as:

Mexican-style rice

Poblano brown rice

black beans

pinto beans

quinoa with vegetables

grilled fajita vegetables

steamed vegetables

broccoli

and:

Yucatan yams .

These are central to Power Plates, bowls, kids meals, and family meals.

They should be reusable components throughout the calculator.

Queso Is Now a Current Menu Component

Current Sharky’s ordering menus prominently include:

Chips & Queso

and:

Poblano Queso .

NutritionSolver currently has no dedicated queso category among its 20 items.

Add verified current nutrition for:

Poblano Queso

and:

Chips & Queso

when available.

Do not assume queso has the same nutrition as shredded cheese.

Nachos Need Size and Protein

Current Sharky’s menus distinguish:

Half Nachos

and:

Nachos Grande ,

with optional protein.

NutritionSolver currently uses:

Nachos Half

and:

Full Nachos .

The current consumer-facing menu name is Nachos Grande , so the database should align its naming with the live menu.

The calculator should use:

Half / Grande → no added protein / chicken / steak / other current option

where supported.

Quesadillas Have Changed

The current menu includes both the standard Quesadilla and a newer Crispy Cheese Quesadilla , which adds a crispy cheese rim, chipotle crema, cotija, and guacamole for dipping.

NutritionSolver currently has no Quesadilla category at all.

That is a significant current-menu gap.

Add:

Quesadilla

Crispy Cheese Quesadilla

and verified protein variants.

Taquitos Are Still Current but the Recipe Label Should Match

Current Sharky’s menus still sell chicken taquitos, including a three-piece restaurant order and dozen-count catering order.

NutritionSolver currently has:

Chicken Taquitos: 810 calories .

Before keeping that number as current, verify whether it represents:

3 taquitos + rice + beans + guacamole + sour cream

from the older complete meal,

or the current:

3 taquitos topped/served with the current accompaniments .

The product name alone is not enough if the included sides have changed.

Salads Need Current Full and Half Logic

Current restaurant menus include:

BBQ Chicken Salad

Tostada Salad

Sharky’s Chicken Salad

Half Sharky’s Chicken Salad

NuMex Caesar Salad

Half NuMex Caesar Salad

and Chicken Tortilla Soup.

NutritionSolver currently has only:

BBQ Chicken Salad

and:

NuMex Caesar Salad .

That misses both current half portions and several major salads.

Sharky’s Chicken Salad Is a Major Omission

The current Chicken Salad uses chicken, greens, cabbage, mandarin oranges, carrots, sesame, almonds or other current crunchy components, green onion, and sesame-lime dressing depending on the current recipe/location.

It is one of the brand’s established salads and appears on current catering menus as well.

It should be a first-class current record.

Tostada Salad Should Return to the Main Dataset

The current menu still lists Tostada Salad with:

organic greens

fajita vegetables

rice

beans

carrots

tomatoes

guacamole

sour cream

pico

cheese

and a crispy tortilla.

NutritionSolver’s current 20-item list omits it completely.

That is a major gap because the older official Sharky’s nutrition menu also specifically published Tostada nutrition.

Chicken Tortilla Soup Is Missing

Current menus still list Chicken Tortilla Soup.

The older official menu published it as a distinct nutrition item as well.

NutritionSolver currently has no Soup category.

Add the current soup serving with an explicit serving size.

Plant-Based Meals Need Their Own Section

Current Sharky’s ordering menus include a dedicated Plant Based section containing options such as:

Achiote Grilled Tofu & Veggie Burrito

AJ Burrito

and:

Achiote Grilled Tofu & Veggie Taco .

The current NutritionSolver page has no Plant-Based category.

This misses one of Sharky’s most brand-specific menu areas, particularly because Sharky’s explicitly promotes organic, non-GMO tofu.

The AJ Burrito Needs Current Coverage

Sharky’s FAQ identifies the AJ Burrito or AJ Bowl as a vegan option built from brown rice, beans, steamed broccoli, and guacamole.

It also remains present in current ordering menus.

This is valuable for exact search intent such as:

Sharky’s AJ Burrito calories

and should be added once its current official nutrition is verified.

Kids Meals Need More Than Three Records

NutritionSolver currently contains:

Kid’s Bowl

Kid’s Cheese Quesadilla

Kid’s Power Plate .

Current restaurant menus additionally include:

Kid’s Organic Bean & Cheese Burrito

Kids Drinks

and:

Kid Churro Bites , with some locations also listing other kids products.

Expand the category.

Kids Bowl Must Preserve the Protein Choice

The current Kid’s Bowl can use:

chicken

tofu

or:

salmon

with rice and beans.

Those three bowls should not all share one fixed nutrition value.

Use:

Kid’s Bowl → Protein → Rice/Beans configuration

where current official component data supports it.

Current Refreshers Are Completely Missing

Sharky’s is currently promoting handcrafted drinks including:

Vanilla Cream Cold Brew Refresher

Mango Mandarin Lemonade Refresher

Mixed Berry Lemonade Refresher

and:

Strawberry Hibiscus Lemonade Refresher on current ordering menus.

NutritionSolver currently has zero beverage records .

That is a significant current-menu gap.

If Sharky’s official nutrition calculator has not published current values for them, list the products with N/A rather than assigning guessed lemonade calories.

Family Meals Need Shared-Order Logic

Current Sharky’s family options include:

Fajita Taco Fiesta for 4

Taco Box

Burrito Box

and:

Family Meal .

The current Family Meal contains approximately:

1.25 lb chicken or steak

16 oz rice

16 oz black beans

side salad

corn and flour tortillas

two 8 oz salsa containers

and chips,

and is intended to feed roughly 3 to 5 people .

That is not one individual serving.

NutritionSolver should support:

Whole meal

and:

My portion

for these items.

Taco Box and Burrito Box Are Group Products

The current Taco Box contains twelve tacos plus sauces and chips, while the Burrito Box contains four Fiesta Burritos plus salsa and chips. Both are designed for several people.

Do not allow these records to distort individual entrée averages.

Place them under:

Family & Group Meals .

Catering Needs Its Own Mode

Sharky’s also has current catering options including:

Fajita Bar

Power Plate Bar

Burrito Party Packs

Taco Party Packs

salad trays

Quesadilla Grande

Taquitos

and group-sized rice, beans, salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.

These should not appear beside one individual taco as though the serving context were equivalent.

Sharky’s Nutrition Questions

How many calories are in a Sharky’s Fiesta Burrito?+
How many calories are in Sharky’s Chicken Lettuce Wraps?+
Does Sharky’s have Power Plates?+
Does Sharky’s have salmon?+
Does Sharky’s have vegan options?+
Does Sharky’s publish nutrition information?+
Are Sharky’s calories exact?+

Calculate Sharky’s in the Same Order the Meal Is Built

For a burrito , choose:

Recipe → Protein → Tortilla → Supported modifications

For tacos :

Taco style → Protein/preparation → Tortilla → Quantity → Sides if ordered as a plate

For a Power Plate :

Protein → Portion → Side 1 → Side 2 → additional side where applicable

For salads :

Full/Half → Protein → Dressing and modifications

Then add any:

queso, chips, guacamole, salsa, drink, dessert, or extra side .

For family or catering meals, calculate the entire order first and then estimate the amount personally eaten.

Sharky’s already provides component-oriented nutrition tools. NutritionSolver can make that information substantially easier to use by preserving the restaurant’s real meal structure instead of reducing a highly customizable menu to twenty fixed cards.

faqs.q: How many calories are in a Sharky’s Fiesta Burrito?
faqs.a:
NutritionSolver currently lists
    

     950 calories
    

     , but Sharky’s has historically published the Fiesta as a range that varied with protein and tortilla selection. Current customization should therefore be verified through Sharky’s interactive nutrition calculator rather than treated as one universal value.

faqs.q: How many calories are in Sharky’s Chicken Lettuce Wraps?
faqs.a:

     400 calories and 37g protein
    

     . An older official Sharky’s menu also published
    

     400 calories and 37g protein
    

     for the standard recipe, which strongly supports the provenance of that particular value.
